analysis: Examined all units. (1) DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift head 779-1116: test-only changes. They cover assistant discovery and fallback, the widening quote, a strict codec for tensorAssistant, and public-traffic text. The tests assert that a plan with the speculative assistant is not called qualified for public traffic (head 960-964). No runtime change is visible here. The production ClusterPublicModels and ClusterConfiguration.validate code is not supplied. (2) scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh (new, 1-37): this is a release tool. It runs the app's own CLI under env -i with a scratch HOME (head 29-31). It then calls the Python fetcher and writes cluster-runtime.json. mkdir refuses an existing folder (28). No new provider runtime surface is visible. (3) scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py (new, 1-226): reads the catalog and manifests from the environment's coordinator and CDN, both from provider-identity.json. Redirects are refused (55-57), responses are size-capped (68-77), and 4xx is not retried. config.json is pinned to the manifest's size and SHA-256 (163-165), and modalities are validated (125-131). The CDN manifest is checked only for model_id and aggregate fields; the app's worker chooses among candidates. r2_prefix is not checked for '..', but it comes from the trusted coordinator catalog. Output folders use numeric names, so there is no path injection. (4) scripts/provider-release-publication.py: adds an optional cluster_runtime block to POST /v1/releases, sent under RELEASE_KEY (A-005). The block is checked for strict shape, canonical form, no duplicate keys, a 64 KiB bound, derived-ID length, and total body size (head 215-228). registration_body changes JSON separators only when the block is present. No validation is weakened. Integration question, not proven here: the release-key-authenticated registration now carries pair_serving_grant and parity_qualifications, including a promotable flag and evidence_sha256. A coordinator turns these into release/<v>/<model>/s<n> approvals and grants. That could merge release publication with qualification authority (A-017, T-054, TB-011, A-011). The backend handling is platform-owned and not supplied. Someone should verify that the coordinator does not treat release-key-supplied qualifications as independent approval. The threat model may also need a cluster-runtime release entry. No concrete regression was identified in the supplied source.
